<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the top-level of the PKGBUILD and does not execute functions such as `pkgver()`, `build()`, or `package()`. In this file, all variable assignments are static or use simple shell expansions that do not involve command substitution or external executions. The `source` array contains a standard Git URL referencing the project's own upstream repository, which is expected for a `-git` package. There are no top-level commands, command substitutions, or dynamic evaluations (like `$(...)` or backticks) outside of function definitions that would be executed during sourcing.

The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry is normal for VCS-based packages and does not pose a risk at this stage, as no download or verification occurs during `--printsrcinfo`. The use of `cd` and `git describe` inside the `pkgver()` function is irrelevant here because function bodies are not evaluated during this phase. No data exfiltration, remote code execution, or suspicious operations occur at parse time.

Thus, merely sourcing this PKGBUILD for metadata extraction poses no security risk.
</details>

The PKGBUILD is for `tio-git`, a serial device I/O tool hosted at the official upstream repository https://github.com/tio/tio. The source is fetched via git from this trusted upstream, which is standard practice for `-git` packages in the AUR. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry is expected and acceptable here because the source is a VCS (git) checkout; reproducibility is handled by the commit referenced in `pkgver`, not by checksums.

The `pkgver()` function uses `git describe --tags --long` to generate a version string based on the latest tag, which is a common and safe method for versioning git packages. The build process uses `meson`, a standard build system, with appropriate flags for prefix and build type. It compiles and installs into the package directory using standard `meson install`. No suspicious commands (e.g., `curl|bash`, `eval`, obfuscated code, or remote downloads) are present.

There are no post-install hooks or system modifications beyond what is necessary to install the software. The package depends only on `glib2` and `lua`, both of which are reasonable for the application's functionality. All operations are confined to the build and package directories. No data exfiltration, unexpected network activity, or dangerous operations are present.
</details>

The package depends on common, legitimate libraries (`glib2`, `lua`) and uses standard build tools (`meson`, `git`).
